title: PH envoy Romualdez: US won't initiate Pax Silica talks during ASEAN meetings
summary: United States President Donald Trump will not discuss the US-led Pax Silica initiative during his bilateral meeting with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos, Jr. and other meetings amid the ongoing…

blocks.text: United States President Donald Trump will not discuss the US-led Pax Silica initiative during his bilateral meeting with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos, Jr. and other meetings amid the ongoing 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits, Philippine Ambassador to the US Jose Manuel Romualdez said.
Romualdez, in a Super Radyo dzBB interview, said the US has given the Philippines time to determine the fine print and coverage of the Pax Silica.

“Ang US ang nagsabi sa atin na hindi muna natin pag-usapan 'yan dahil dapat ayusin muna kung anong agreement na puwede natin pasukan, kung ano 'yung hinihingi nila, at kung ano 'yung puwede sa atin,” Romualdez said.
(The US told us that it will not be discussed yet because there is a need to check first the agreement that will be entered into, what they were asking from us, and what is acceptable to us.)
“President Marcos wants the process to be transparent,” he added.

A House bill establishing an economic zone for the Pax Silica initiative has been filed, but the measure is yet to be comprehensively discussed amid the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte and ongoing deliberations on the proposed P7.2 trillion national budget for 2027.

The bill provides that the Advanced Industries Zone will serve as “the country's national platform for strategic technology, advanced manufacturing, and innovation, under a dedicated authority empowered to attract investment and deliver government services efficiently.”

In return for competitive incentives, the bill states that enterprises or locators in the Advanced Industries Zone must create jobs for Filipinos, train Filipino workers, and transfer skills and know-how, so that Filipinos will not only assemble these technologies but ultimately design, build, and manage them later on.

Over 200 individuals, however, were arrested over the weekend due to protests against Trump and Pax Silica, mainly due to concerns raised by the indigenous people that they will be displaced from their ancestral domain.
The authors of the bill establishing the ecozone earlier said that the initiative will only cover the government’s patrimonial land.
Romualdez said protests and questions about the initiative are proof that sealing the Pax Silica deal is not something that can be rushed.
“It would be better if we are not doing this in haste,” he said.
The main issue for the Trump-Marcos meeting, Romualdez said, remains the completion of the Code of Conduct on the South China Sea between ASEAN and China.
The US supports freedom of navigation in the area in accordance with international law and has an existing mutual defense treaty with the Philippines since 1952.
“That Code of Conduct is the priority, and our future in the digital world,” Romualdez added. —AOL, GMA News
